title: PURE: Usability Scores From Experts
intro: PURE turns expert review into a number you can compare across versions and competitors.

learn.title: How a PURE review runs
learn.text:
**1. Define tasks** — the primary tasks for a target user
**2. Break into steps** — what the user does, in order
**3. Rate each step** — several experts rate difficulty independently
**4. Sum and compare** — a task score and a product score you can track over time

Pragmatic Usability Rating by Experts: structured enough to be comparable, cheap enough to run often.

try.explain: Scores you can track across versions and against competitors.

learn.title: The 5-point scale
learn.text:
The original 3-point scale — easy / some difficulty / high difficulty — was **too coarse for elaborate workflows**.

With help from PURE co-creator Christian Rohrer, Calabro trialled a 5-point version: 14 researchers, 24 evaluations across CAD simulation products.

The two new anchors — **frictionless** at one end and **critical error** at the other — made scoring faster and easier, according to the evaluators.

try.q: What did adding two anchors to the scale achieve?
options: Evaluators found scoring faster and easier
It removed the need for multiple raters
It doubled the number of tasks covered
It made scores comparable with SUS
try.explain: Frictionless and critical error gave the extremes a definition.

learn.title: What it's for
learn.text:
Calabro has seen PURE raise quality across **seven teams**: it gives a shared vocabulary for difficulty and makes regressions visible between releases.

It is an expert method, so it tells you what trained evaluators predict — not what users did. Use it to prioritise and to track, then confirm the risky steps with real people.

try.q: What does a PURE score represent?
try.explain: It is expert judgement, structured and summed.

test.explain: Expert ratings, turned into a comparable number.

test.q: Why did the 3-point scale need extending?
options: It was too coarse for elaborate workflows
It couldn't produce a product score

test.explain: 14 researchers, 24 evaluations across CAD simulation products.

test.q: How many experts should rate each step?
test.explain: Independent ratings are what make the score trustworthy.

test.q: What should follow a PURE review?
options: Confirming the risky steps with users
A redesign of the lowest-scoring task
A second review by the same experts
test.explain: Expert prediction prioritises; user evidence confirms.
